newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Asian dealers see copper stuck in sideways trade.
newsitem.headline: Asian dealers see copper stuck in sideways trade.

text.p: Three-month copper on the London Metal Exchange (LME) is seen swinging sideways until the end of the Easter holidays, Far East traders said on Thursday.
"We expect no big move this week due to the long holiday," a trader at one local brokerage firm said.
"A range of US$2,320 to $2,380 (a tonne) has worked well so far, acting like a magnet to get copper back into its range," the trader said.
Three-month copper fell by $3 a tonne and was seen at $2,345/50 in late Asian trading on Thursday from yesterday's London quote of $2,348/53 a tonne.
Three-month zinc prices were also seen falling on technical factors as the trade pulled back from an overbought situation, traders said.

A futures broker said the heavily overbought situation in the zinc market eased slightly with the 14-day relative strength index (RSI) for three-month zinc standing at 64.90 percent, compared with 70.99 percent the previous day.
The market generally considers an RSI of 70 or more as overbought and 30 or less as oversold.
Zinc climbed to a 4-1/2 year high last week at $1,307 a tonne before sliding back to its current level. Zinc closed late on Wednesday in the LME at $1,280/84 a tonne.
Three-month aluminium fell by $2 a tonne in Asian trade against the late London trade of $1,637/40 a tonne.
The futures broker pegged resistance for three-month aluminium at $1,669 and support at $1,625 a tonne.
